scores.notes: Jesus stands in the bright cave mouth with his hand raised and Martha kneels at centre, but Lazarus already sits upright and unbound-faced on a stone bench among the mourners at left inside the tomb rather than stirring at its dark back, which contradicts the moment of the call. A second seated woman at right reads as part of the crowd.

Moses holds his rod aloft beside the split rock as water gushes into a pool. Aaron in ephod and breastplate stands beside him, goats and sheep drink at left and centre, and the people kneel with jars at right before the tents; no glyphs or edge problems.

Alice sits centred with her chin on her hand under a great tree, with the hatted, waistcoated March Hare, the Hatter and the Dormouse asleep on a plate at right. The card in the Hatter's hat carries only a dotted pattern with no legible characters, and the watercolour runs to every edge.

Saul half-rises from a carved chair at left with his throwing arm flung back as the spear crosses the stone hall, and young David dodges at right with the lyre at his feet and lamp stands burning. No figure is drawn for the evil spirit.

Holmes's face and curly hair closely resemble Benedict Cumberbatch's screen Sherlock. The framed certificate at top left bears a script heading resembling 'Sherlock Holmes' with lines of text, and the papers pinned at upper right carry handwriting-like marks.

Holmes at the carriage window is a clear Benedict Cumberbatch likeness and the bowler-hatted man beside him resembles Martin Freeman, both borrowed from the BBC adaptation. Otherwise the scene reads well: the bandaged Hatherley, Bradstreet leaning out, the waving station-master and the fire column at right; his paper shows only a ruled grid.

The burning whitewashed house, horse-drawn fire engines and the travellers with the laughing station-master all match the scene. However, the timetable sheets under the station-master's arm at lower right are covered in rows of text-like lettering.

A woman fills a basket with grapes while a man steadies a vine post. A child carries two water jars, an ox rests by the wall, and a red-cloaked figure walks the road, with the harbour and walled city under a golden, clouded sky; hands and edges are clean.

Two little girls, one a miniature Alice in pinafore, and a baby peek round the left doorway as unrequested figures, and the papers scattered on the floor at lower left carry lines of text. The Queen's black hair, small crown and tall heart-shaped collar follow the Disney Queen of Hearts design.

Aaron in a gem-set breastplate and ephod gestures toward a pig at left while Moses stands beside him with a staff. The crowd gathers at right with the camp and smoking tabernacle behind, and there are no glyphs or anatomical faults.

Moses sits on the stone with both arms upheld, but three helpers surround him: two brown-robed men hold his arms and a third man in ephod and headband stands behind with a hand on his shoulder, one figure more than Aaron and Hur. The battle on the plain at left is fine.

The Levite kneels with a knife over the still, clothed body on a cloth in a mud-brick room, with a lamp on the table, sandals and a cloak set aside, and the donkey in the moonlit doorway. The moment is restrained, with no gore.

Darius leans over a waist-high rim at left, but Daniel and both rope-pulling attendants stand on the same den floor as the lions. The rope trails slack, so Daniel is tugged sideways rather than hauled up and out, which makes the space and action contradictory.

The seraphim are ordinary robed angels with one pair of wings and bare, uncovered feet, and several faces are visible in the background, which breaks the six-winged text. One seraph at upper right holds tongs with a burning coal toward Isaiah, a later verse (6:6). No figure of God appears.

Paul sits on a bench gazing upward with the believers in a circle around him, with tied scrolls and a reed pen beside him, a lamp on the shelf and Corinth seen through the bright doorway. The scrolls show no legible marks and the paint runs to the edges.

Daniel at left raises a declining hand toward Belshazzar on a golden throne at right. A tray with a gold chain sits at the king's feet and the feast hall with glazed-brick lion friezes lies behind; the friezes carry no inscriptions.

Ezekiel stands small in the middle of a valley strewn with skulls and bones, arm raised and holding a closed book with no visible writing. The watercolour vignettes into white paper on all sides, an accepted fault, and no figure is drawn for God.

David follows through with his sling at left while the armoured Goliath reels in a burst of dust, with spear and shield leaving his grasp and both armies on the slopes, and there is no gore. Goliath tips backward rather than onto his face, a small departure.

The Caterpillar is film-style blue with a fully human old man's face, human hands, a waistcoat and a bowler hat that the text does not give, so it is not drawn as an animal. It still has the hookah in its mouth; Alice and the mushroom clearing are otherwise right.

Jesus stands in the boat with an arm stretched over the water while the disciples cling to the gunwales and mast. The sail is torn, a lantern hangs on the mast and the sky breaks toward dawn over the Galilee shore; the watercolour reaches every edge.

Alice holds a flamingo under one arm but swings an ordinary pink croquet mallet, and a metal hoop stands at right, both contradicting live-flamingo mallets and soldier arches. The card soldiers at left are muddled, with one card draped between two men, and the white paper edges at left are accepted.

Rephaiah in a brown cloak stands on scaffolding pointing at the wall while labourers set stones and carry baskets of rubble, and an armoured guard with a spear stands at right before Jerusalem's walls. There are no glyphs or bad hands.

Peter walks on the stormy water toward Jesus with the boat, lantern and disciples at left. However, a young child sits lit by the lantern in the middle of the disciples, a prominent figure the Twelve and the scene do not call for.

Holmes is drawn as a clear Benedict Cumberbatch likeness and Watson resembles Martin Freeman from the BBC series. The square, railings, three gilt balls and a blank brown board are right, and a tiny squiggle on the pavement at lower left reads as a stain rather than writing.

Moses stands on a low rise pointing onward with his staff, while families with bundles, a donkey and sheep spread out behind among tents beneath cloud-wrapped Horeb. The watercolour fades to white paper at the left and corners, an accepted fault.

Moses sits on a stone with Hur holding his right arm and Aaron, in a gem-set breastplate, holding his left, with Israelites and Amalekites fighting on both sides in the late light. The fighting sits closer than the plain below, but hands and figures are sound.
